example.target: La población de la ciudad ha crecido mucho en los últimos años.
example.gloss: The city's population has grown a lot in recent years.

example.target: Mi generación ha vivido muchos cambios tecnológicos.
example.gloss: My generation has experienced many technological changes.

example.target: Pasó su juventud viajando por el mundo.
example.gloss: He spent his youth traveling around the world.

example.target: En su infancia vivía en un pueblo pequeño.
example.gloss: In her childhood she lived in a small village.

example.target: Quiere disfrutar de la vejez con salud y tranquilidad.

example.gloss: That stereotype about young people is not true.

example.gloss: The company has a clear policy against discrimination.

example.target: Hace voluntariado en un centro para personas mayores.
example.gloss: He volunteers at a center for elderly people.

example.gloss: There was a disagreement about how to share out the work.

example.target: Asumió el compromiso de ayudar cada fin de semana.

example.target: El respeto es la base de cualquier relación.
example.gloss: Respect is the basis of any relationship.

example.target: Es una tradición reunir a toda la familia en Navidad.
example.gloss: It is a tradition to gather the whole family at Christmas.

words.note: here in the sense of value or courage, not monetary worth

example.target: Admiro el valor con el que afrontó la enfermedad.
example.gloss: I admire the courage with which she faced the illness.

example.target: Saludar al entrar es una norma social muy extendida.
example.gloss: Greeting people when you enter is a very widespread social norm.

example.target: El barrio es conocido por su diversidad cultural.
example.gloss: The neighborhood is known for its cultural diversity.

words.note: feminine cristiana; also used as a noun, un cristiano

example.target: Mi vecino es cristiano y va a la iglesia los domingos.
example.gloss: My neighbour is Christian and goes to church on Sundays.

words.note: feminine judía; also used as a noun

example.target: Su abuelo es judío y vive en Toledo.
example.gloss: His grandfather is Jewish and lives in Toledo.

words.note: feminine musulmana, without the accent, because the stress falls naturally there

example.target: Mi compañero es musulmán y no come cerdo.
example.gloss: My classmate is Muslim and does not eat pork.

words.note: one form for both genders: un budista, una budista

example.target: Ella es budista y medita todos los días.
example.gloss: She is Buddhist and meditates every day.

example.target: La mezquita está cerca del centro.
example.gloss: The mosque is near the centre.

example.target: Visitamos la sinagoga el sábado por la mañana.
example.gloss: We visited the synagogue on Saturday morning.

example.gloss: Social exclusion mainly affects the most vulnerable.

example.target: A veces la brecha generacional dificulta la comunicación en casa.
example.gloss: Sometimes the generation gap makes communication at home difficult.

example.target: Su amistad ha durado más de veinte años.

example.target: En el equipo hay mucho compañerismo.
example.gloss: There is a lot of camaraderie in the team.

example.target: Valoro la lealtad más que cualquier otra cualidad.
example.gloss: I value loyalty more than any other quality.

example.target: Habló con total sinceridad sobre sus dudas.

example.target: Necesita un poco de intimidad para pensar con calma.

example.target: Le demuestra su afecto con pequeños gestos.

example.target: Trata a sus alumnos con mucho cariño.
example.gloss: She treats her students with a lot of affection.

example.gloss: The bond between the two sisters is very strong.

example.gloss: The breakup was very painful for both of them.

example.target: Guardó el secreto durante muchos años.

words.note: colloquial

example.target: Mis padres siempre me apoyan en mis decisiones.
example.gloss: My parents always support me in my decisions.

words.note: confiar en; irregular accent: confío, confías, confía, confían

example.gloss: I trust you more than anyone.

words.note: fiarse de; pronominal; irregular accent: me fío

example.target: No me fío de la gente que no conozco.
example.gloss: I do not trust people I do not know.

example.target: Nunca traicionaría a un amigo.

example.gloss: I forgive you, but I do not forget it.

words.note: reconciliarse con; pronominal

example.gloss: After the fight, they made up right away.

words.note: irregular past participle: roto

words.note: llevarse bien con; pronominal

example.target: Nos llevamos muy bien con los vecinos.
example.gloss: We get along very well with the neighbors.

words.en: to make a good impression on someone, to like
words.note: works like gustar: me cae bien, me caen bien

words.note: usually plural; takes los

example.gloss: I prefer a sincere friend to one who only says what I want to hear.

example.gloss: It seems hypocritical to me to say one thing and do another.

example.gloss: He has been a loyal friend since childhood.

words.en: to get together, to meet up
words.note: pronominal; juntarse con

words.note: distanciarse de; pronominal

example.gloss: They grew apart after the argument.

example.gloss: The law prohibits discriminating on grounds of origin.

words.note: o>üe: me avergüenzo; avergonzarse de; pronominal

example.gloss: She does not hold a grudge against anyone.

example.target: La empatía nos ayuda a entender a los demás.
example.gloss: Empathy helps us understand other people.

example.target: Trata los temas difíciles con mucha sensibilidad.

words.note: same form for masculine and feminine

example.gloss: She was very brave to tell what had happened to her.

words.note: same form for masculine and feminine

words.note: same form for masculine and feminine

example.gloss: He is too pessimistic about the future.

example.target: Mi hermano es muy extrovertido y habla con todo el mundo.
example.gloss: My brother is very outgoing and talks to everyone.

example.target: Es bastante introvertido y prefiere estar solo.
example.gloss: He is quite introverted and prefers to be alone.

example.gloss: He is still resentful about how they treated him at work.

example.gloss: He shows himself indifferent to criticism.

example.gloss: Her indifference hurt me more than anger would have.

words.note: epicene: el emigrante / la emigrante, invariable in gender

example.gloss: Many emigrants return to their country after a few years.

example.gloss: The team gives him a strong sense of belonging.

example.target: El colectivo de vecinos organizó una fiesta en la plaza.

example.gloss: Social interaction is harder for shy people.

words.note: here in the sense of a thoughtful gesture, not a small detail

example.gloss: She loves doing something nice for her friends.

words.note: o>ue: consuelo, consuela

example.target: Fue a consolar a su amiga después de la mala noticia.
example.gloss: She went to comfort her friend after the bad news.
